chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sharif ibn Sabiq, from Al-Fadl ibn Abi Ghurrah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, foolishness is a lowly character trait; he extends himself (dominates) over those who are below him, and he submits to those who are above him.

key_terms.السَّفَهَ: Foolishness; lack of wisdom or sound judgment, often implying moral deficiency.
key_terms.يَسْتَطِيلُ: He extends himself; implies dominating or looking down upon.

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of foolishness (Safah) in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) characterizes *al-safah* (foolishness) as a distinct moral vice of social opportunism rather than mere intellectual deficiency. He describes the fool as possessing a 'base character' that manifests as arrogance towards inferiors and subservience to superiors, a concept deeply rooted in Shia ethical teachings on *adab* (etiquette) and self-awareness. This definition highlights how true wisdom requires consistency in demeanor regardless of social hierarchy, contrasting with the hypocritical fluctuation of the foolish.
